newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee firms up as call rates rise.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee firms up as call rates rise.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee firmed in early trade on Tuesday as call money rates rose due to tightness in the money market, dealers said.
At 0440 GMT the rupee was at 57.72 to the dollar, after opening at 57.85. The rupee closed at 57.87 on Monday.
Dearlers said the dollar-rupee exchange rate fell in the morning despite the Central Bank pushing up the dollar by 3.5 local cents. Buying and selling prices were set at 56.7592 and 57.9058.
Overnight call money was up on tight supply as banks have been covering import requirement with dollars from the Central Bank since last Thursday, dealers said.
Call rates were at 18 percent, after opening at 16.
"Last Thursday and Friday alone the Central Bank sold dollars worth 875 million rupees," said a Union Bank dealer.
The Central Bank was expected to inject liquidity back into the system by buying 500 million rupees worth of Treasury Bills at tomorrow's auction, he said.
Dealers expect the dollar to remain depressed until call rates settle.
